title: Translation Validation Procedures
body:

Validates translations by checking meaning preservation, terminology consistency, and back-translation agreement. It belongs to the shared capability infrastructure: it is not a disconnected list, but one catalog entry in a system where databases link to each other, share search and validation rules, and can be checked against related databases. Its teaching ladder rank is simple, so it is placed where a reader working from simple records toward compounded and most complex records will meet it at the right point in the sequence.

Scope and schema. The scope of this record is exactly one well defined piece of language understanding: translation validation procedures. Every record in this database carries the same schema fields: id, title, scope, schema, method, checks, demo, evidence, version, and provenance. The scope field states what the record covers and what it deliberately does not cover; the schema field lists the data the record must contain before it is accepted; the method field names the procedure applied; the checks field lists the acceptance tests the result must pass. A record missing any required field is rejected at build time, not published with a gap.

Method. The working method for this record is Translation validation and terminology checking. First, the question is written down in one sentence so its scope is clear. Second, the relevant inputs and assumptions are listed, including anything that is not yet known. Third, the method is applied in order, with each intermediate result kept visible rather than hidden inside a single final number. Fourth, the result is compared against an independent check, such as a second calculation, a boundary case, or a review of the assumptions. If the check disagrees, the record says so and the disagreement is investigated before the record is marked complete.

Search and retrieval. This record is retrievable by its title, its record ID, and any word in its body, through the search box on the database page and through the synonym map, which expands a query term to its listed relatives before matching. Retrieval was measured at build time on this database's own records: every record title query returns its record, and every record loads and parses. That measurement is reported as a build time result on this database's own data, not as a claim about any other system.

Validation and acceptance tests. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness (all required fields present), field consistency (ID prefix, edition, and source label agree), teaching ladder placement (all three tiers present in the database), and demo re-execution (the demo program run again and its stdout compared byte for byte with the stored demo output). The acceptance test for this record is that all four checks pass; a record failing any one of them is not published. Versioning, access, and provenance: each record carries a version (1.0 at initial build), a source label, and a last verified date, so a later reviewer can tell what changed, when, and from what source.
